'''Mykhailo Ulyanovych Bilyi''' ({{langx|uk|Михайло Улянович Білий}}; 12 November 1922&nbsp;– 5 August 2001) was a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] and [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] physicist and politician, who served as the [[Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada]] of the [[Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic]] from 1972 to 1980. Since 1969 he was a Corresponding Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] (then the Academy of Sciences of Ukrainian SSR).

==Biography==
Mykhailo Bilyi was born on 12 November 1922 in the village of Moskali that today is located in [[Chernihiv Raion]], [[Northern Ukraine]] into a peasant family.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Matviĭchuk |first1=Olena |title=Ky·ivs·kyj Nacional·nyj Universytet Imeni Tarasa Ševčenka: Imena slavnych sučasnykiv |date=2004 |publisher=Svit Uspikhu |isbn=978-966-8352-00-3 |page=28 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Ky_ivs_kyj_Nacional_nyj_Universytet_Imen/Z6glAQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=%D0%9C%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%BE+%D0%A3%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87+%D0%91%D1%96%D0%BB%D0%B8+%2212+%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B0+1922%22&dq=%D0%9C%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%BE+%D0%A3%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87+%D0%91%D1%96%D0%BB%D0%B8+%2212+%D0%BB%D0%B8%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%B4%D0%B0+1922%22&printsec=frontcover |access-date=16 January 2026 |language=uk}}</ref> After graduating from primary school, he served in the [[Red Army]], and served during [[World War II]] within the [[Transcaucasian Military District]].<ref name="k">{{cite web |title=Білий Михайло Ульянович |url=https://knu.ua/ua/geninf/history-rectors/bilii/ |website=knu.ua |access-date=16 January 2026}}</ref> However, he was wounded and had to be treated in [[Baku]] in May 1943, and thereafter did not return to military service.<ref name="k" /> Starting in 1944, he entered the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics at [[Azerbaijan University]], but transferred in the following year to the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics from [[Kyiv University]].<ref name="k" />

In 1951, after defendeed his dissertation on the spectra of absorportion of solutions of lead salts to receive his degree of Candidate of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, he began working as a professor at Kyiv University.<ref name="k" /> In 1962 he was promoted to the Dean of the Faculty of Physics at Kyiv University, which he served as until 1970.<ref>{{cite book |title=Український фізичний журнал |date=2001 |publisher=Наук. думка |page=1311 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%97%D0%BD%D1%81%D1%8C%D0%BA%D0%B8%D0%B9_%D1%84%D1%96%D0%B7%D0%B8%D1%87%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B9/u6jyAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=%D0%9C%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%BE+%D0%A3%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87+%D0%91%D1%96%D0%BB%D0%B8+%221962%22&dq=%D0%9C%D0%B8%D1%85%D0%B0%D0%B9%D0%BB%D0%BE+%D0%A3%D0%BB%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87+%D0%91%D1%96%D0%BB%D0%B8+%221962%22&printsec=frontcover |access-date=16 January 2026 |language=uk}}</ref> During this time, he became a Corresponding Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]].<ref name="k" /> He then became Rector of Kyiv University, a position he held for 15 years until 1985.<ref name="k" />
